views.name: orders_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  store_id,
  channel_id,
  payment_order_id,
  delivery_order_id,
  order_status,
  order_amount,
  order_delivery_fee,
  order_delivery_cost,
  order_created_hour,
  order_created_minute,
  order_created_day,
  order_created_month,
  order_created_year,
  order_moment_created,
  order_moment_accepted,
  order_moment_ready,
  order_moment_collected,
  order_moment_in_expedition,
  order_moment_delivering,
  order_moment_delivered,
  order_moment_finished,
  COALESCE(order_metric_collected_time, 0.0) AS order_metric_collected_time,
  COALESCE(order_metric_paused_time, 0.0) AS order_metric_paused_time,
  COALESCE(order_metric_production_time, 0.0) AS order_metric_production_time,
  COALESCE(order_metric_walking_time, 0.0) AS order_metric_walking_time,
  COALESCE(order_metric_expediton_speed_time, 0.0) AS order_metric_expediton_speed_time,
  COALESCE(order_metric_transit_time, 0.0) AS order_metric_transit_time,
  COALESCE(order_metric_cycle_time, 0.0) AS order_metric_cycle_time
FROM orders
views.description: Normalized orders row with canonical timestamp and key columns preserved. Use this as the cleaned order-level base for joins, time-based calculations, and filtering cohorts. It exposes original order columns and standardizes NULL-safe copies of event timestamps and numeric metrics. | Use for: time-to-event calculations using order_moment_* timestamps; per-order metric aggregations and joins to payments/deliveries/stores; cohort selection by order_status or created date parts

views.name: payments_rolled
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  payment_order_id,
  SUM(COALESCE(payment_amount, 0.0)) AS total_payment_amount,
  SUM(COALESCE(payment_fee, 0.0)) AS total_payment_fee,
  COUNT(payment_id) AS payment_count
FROM payments
GROUP BY payment_order_id
views.description: Aggregate payments at the payment_order_id (order-level) to get total paid amount, total fees and count of payment records per order. Useful when orders may have multiple payments or fees and you need one row per order with payment totals. | Use for: order-level revenue and fee calculations; reconciling payments to orders; detecting orders with multiple payments or missing payments

views.name: deliveries_with_driver
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.delivery_id,
  d.delivery_order_id,
  d.driver_id,
  d.delivery_distance_meters,
  d.delivery_status,
  dr.driver_modal,
  dr.driver_type
FROM deliveries d
LEFT JOIN drivers dr
  ON d.driver_id = dr.driver_id
views.description: Denormalized deliveries enriched with driver attributes. One row per delivery including delivery measures and driver descriptive columns. Useful for driver performance, distance analysis, and joining deliveries back to orders via delivery_order_id. | Use for: average delivery distance by driver type or modal; join deliveries to orders to assess delivery outcomes by driver attributes; filtering deliveries by delivery_status with driver info

views.name: stores_with_hub
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.store_id,
  s.hub_id,
  s.store_name,
  s.store_segment,
  s.store_plan_price,
  s.store_latitude,
  s.store_longitude,
  h.hub_name,
  h.hub_city,
  h.hub_state,
  h.hub_latitude,
  h.hub_longitude
FROM stores s
LEFT JOIN hubs h
  ON s.hub_id = h.hub_id
views.description: Store dimension enriched with its hub attributes. One row per store including geographic and hub descriptors. Use for geospatial grouping, store-level rollups, and joining to orders. | Use for: store-level geographic analyses; aggregations by hub attributes (city/state); joining orders to hub-level meta

views.name: orders_enriched
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.store_id,
  s.store_name,
  s.store_segment,
  s.store_plan_price,
  s.store_latitude,
  s.store_longitude,
  s.hub_id,
  h.hub_name,
  h.hub_city,
  h.hub_state,
  o.channel_id,
  c.channel_name,
  c.channel_type,
  o.payment_order_id,
  p.total_payment_amount,
  p.total_payment_fee,
  p.payment_count,
  o.delivery_order_id,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_amount,
  o.order_delivery_fee,
  o.order_delivery_cost,
  o.order_moment_created,
  o.order_moment_accepted,
  o.order_moment_ready,
  o.order_moment_collected,
  o.order_moment_in_expedition,
  o.order_moment_delivering,
  o.order_moment_delivered,
  o.order_moment_finished,
  o.order_metric_collected_time,
  o.order_metric_paused_time,
  o.order_metric_production_time,
  o.order_metric_walking_time,
  o.order_metric_expediton_speed_time,
  o.order_metric_transit_time,
  o.order_metric_cycle_time
FROM orders_base o
LEFT JOIN stores_with_hub s
  ON o.store_id = s.store_id
LEFT JOIN hubs h
  ON s.hub_id = h.hub_id
LEFT JOIN channels c
  ON o.channel_id = c.channel_id
LEFT JOIN payments_rolled p
  ON o.payment_order_id = p.payment_order_id
views.description: Wide denormalized order-level relation joining orders to stores (with hub), channel and aggregated payments. Preserves order grain and key columns needed for analytics. Use as a one-stop table for order-level reporting combining store, hub, channel and payment totals. | Use for: order-level revenue and lifecycle analysis; join orders to deliveries/drivers and compute KPIs by store/hub/channel; filter by order_status and aggregate metrics

views.name: orders_by_day
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_created_year,
  order_created_month,
  order_created_day,
  COUNT(order_id) AS orders_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(order_amount, 0.0)) AS total_order_amount,
  SUM(COALESCE(order_delivery_fee, 0.0)) AS total_delivery_fee,
  SUM(COALESCE(order_delivery_cost, 0.0)) AS total_delivery_cost
FROM orders
GROUP BY order_created_year, order_created_month, order_created_day
views.description: Daily aggregates of orders by calendar day (based on order_created_year/month/day) with counts and sums. Useful for time-series trends, daily dashboards, and further time-window analytics. Keeps year/month/day as grouping keys. | Use for: daily trend reports of orders and revenue; detecting anomalies in daily volumes or fees; feeding downstream time-series visualizations

views.name: latest_delivery_per_order
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  delivery_order_id,
  delivery_id,
  driver_id,
  delivery_distance_meters,
  delivery_status
FROM (
  SELECT
    delivery_order_id,
    delivery_id,
    driver_id,
    delivery_distance_meters,
    delivery_status,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY delivery_order_id ORDER BY delivery_id DESC) AS rn
  FROM deliveries
) WHERE rn = 1
views.description: For each delivery_order_id (order), pick the delivery row with the max delivery_id (deterministic latest by delivery_id). Returns one row per delivery_order_id including delivery and driver reference. Use when orders may have multiple delivery attempts and a single representative delivery row is needed. | Use for: attach a single delivery record to orders for analysis; analyze the latest delivery outcome per order; join to drivers for last-attempt performance

views.name: channel_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.channel_id,
  COUNT(o.order_id) AS orders_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(o.order_amount, 0.0)) AS total_order_amount,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(o.order_id) = 0 THEN 0 ELSE SUM(COALESCE(o.order_amount, 0.0)) * 1.0 / COUNT(o.order_id) END AS avg_order_amount
FROM orders o
GROUP BY o.channel_id
views.description: Aggregated metrics per channel_id: number of orders, total order amount and average order amount. Useful for comparing channel performance and funnel analysis. | Use for: compare channel contribution to revenue; derive average basket size by channel; identify channels with low/high order counts
